timeline_features: dated sequence with explicit uncertainty notes
branch point that changes downstream history
counterfactual divergence from an established baseline
multiple event scales from single choice to war-level consequence
later events retain ancestry to the divergence point
rift_features: space-time rupture associated with a high-impact event
different concentrations produce different pull effects
force-bleed or nexus locations can be tracked separately
failed repair attempts can worsen a rupture
remote rupture points may require dedicated receiving/research stations
arrival_features: arrival may include memory loss or incomplete self-context
initial observation should precede identity conclusions
movement and access may be constrained while assessment is active
multiple observers can disagree about the meaning or risk of an arrival
assessment history should preserve disagreement rather than flatten it

universal_codex_translation.timeline_rule: A timeline view should preserve branch ancestry, divergence points, and uncertainty instead of rewriting alternate history into one flat sequence.
universal_codex_translation.uncertainty_rule: Approximate or disputed dates remain visibly approximate or disputed.
universal_codex_translation.arrival_rule: Incomplete memory or context must not be filled by system inference as if recalled fact.
universal_codex_translation.repair_rule: A repair attempt is itself an event with consequences and may worsen the state; record before/after rather than assuming repair success.
